### A Beautiful Bride
Author: Gwen Smith
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/girlfriends/girlfriends-in-god-june-2-2022.html
Passage: Psalm 45:14
Points:
- Earthly weddings reflect joy, radiant beauty, and joyful anticipation.
- The extravagant wedding celebration in Psalm 45 foreshadows Christ and His bride.
- The bride of Christ is adorned from within with spiritual fruit and virtue.
- Believers can live with royal confidence knowing they are deeply cherished by Jesus.
- The anticipation of Christ's return prompts believers to prepare their hearts in holiness.

### Wisdom from the Psalms 4/19
Author: Barbour Publishing
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/wisdom/wisdom-from-the-psalms-4-or-19-552276.html
Passage: Psalm 45:17
Points:
- A craftsman contemplates the finest possible monument he could carve out of stone.
- Human accomplishments and self-monuments pale beside the majesty of creation.
- The highest enduring legacy anyone can offer is honoring the name of God.
- Believers are invited to make their lives a living testimony of praise for future generations.

### The King's Glorious Bride
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/kings-glorious-bride
Passage: Psalm 45:10-17
Points:
- The queen is urged to leave behind past loyalties to join the royal household.
- Her calling mirrors the church forsaking worldly idols to submit wholly to Jesus.
- Any beauty, honor, or royal standing the bride possesses is given by the King.
- Christ continually sanctifies His people even when personal spiritual growth feels slow.
- Believers stand secure because they are robed in the perfect righteousness of Christ.

### Read the Bible: Psalm 45
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/1-samuel-28-1-corinthians-9-ezekiel-7-psalm-45/
Passage: Psalm 45:1-17
Points:
- Psalm 45 functions historically as a royal wedding song celebrating a Davidic monarch.
- The psalm highlights a ruler characterized by military strength alongside truth and humility.
- The poet addresses the king in exalted terms while maintaining a distinction from God Himself.
- Hebrews applies this language typologically to Jesus to establish His superiority over angels.
- Christ stands as the ultimate Davidic King whose throne and kingdom endure forever.
